topic: The Geometric Intuition of the Cross Product

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors in 3D Space
lecture_lines: Consider two vectors, u and v, in 3D.
They define a parallelogram in space.
This shape is our geometric foundation.
animations: Label the x, y, z axes clearly using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/axis.svg].
Represent a vector v as an arrow from origin [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/origin.svg].

sections.title: Definition of the Cross Product
lecture_lines: The cross product creates a new vector.
This vector is perpendicular to the plane.
Its magnitude equals the parallelogram's area.
animations: Show two vectors a and b in space, arranged to form a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/parallelogram.svg].
Draw a resultant vector c perpendicular to a and b.
Label c as the cross product a x b.

sections.title: Geometric Intuition & Determinants
lecture_lines: The cross product is a determinant.
Zero area means vectors are collinear.
It measures how independent vectors are.
animations: Display a 2D parallelogram formed by vectors a and b.
Highlight the area represented by the cross product magnitude.
Show the determinant formula for the cross product area.
Illustrate the right-hand rule for the resulting vector direction using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/hand.svg].
Animate the change in area as vectors a and b rotate.

sections.title: Linear Transformations and Orientation
lecture_lines: They map vectors to a new space.
animations: Show a grid transformation matrix [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg] applying to basis vectors.
Illustrate the change in volume/orientation from transformation.
Highlight the cross product as a linear transformation property using basis vectors [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/vector.svg].

sections.title: Summary & Application
lecture_lines: Cross product equals perpendicular vector area.
It is crucial for calculating torque.
Force times lever arm yields rotation.
animations: Summarize key points: vector definition, formula, and geometry. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/wrench.svg]
Highlight the cross product in physics/engineering applications. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/engine.svg]
Review the orientation-dependent nature of the cross product. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/lever.svg]
